title: Service Mesh Deep Dive
summary: A service mesh inserts a data plane (usually Envoy sidecars or ambient proxies) to provide mTLS, retries, timeouts, observability, and traffic splitting uniformly — at the cost of complexity and latency.

sections.title: Problem statement
paragraphs: Microservices reimplement RPC concerns inconsistently. A mesh centralizes policy in proxies next to workloads or on nodes.
Control planes (Istio, Linkerd, Consul) push configuration; data planes carry traffic.

sections.title: Features that matter
paragraphs: mTLS identity, retries with budgets, timeouts, outlier detection, canaries, and golden signals telemetry.
Ambition creep — turning the mesh into a business-rules engine — creates opaque failure domains.

sections.title: Costs
paragraphs: Sidecar CPU/RAM, added hops, upgrade coupling, and debugging difficulty. Ambient/mode alternatives reduce per-pod sidecars but change trust boundaries.

sections.title: When to adopt
paragraphs: Adopt when you have many services needing uniform security/telemetry and a platform team to own it. Skip for small monolith-adjacent estates.

deepDive.title: Service Mesh Deep Dive — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Service Mesh Deep Dive in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Service Mesh Deep Dive — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Service Mesh Deep Dive include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Service Mesh Deep Dive — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Service Mesh Deep Dive intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

practices: Own the mesh as a platform product
keyTakeaways: Complexity must be justified by estate size
whyItMatters: Service mesh decisions shape security and reliability for years; they are hard to undo.
reflectionQuestions: Which mesh features do you truly need in the next year?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
